items.title: ET-CSS
items.oneLiner: My utility-first framework, years before Tailwind went mainstream.
items.detail: 605 lines of Sass. Set colors, breakpoints and ranges as variables; loops generate spacing, color, type, border, sizing, display and overflow utilities with responsive suffixes. It ran on several Movistar Ecuador sites in production. Not perfect: no grid, and one duplicated class I'd fix today.

items.title: How the hero was made
items.oneLiner: From scanned paper cutouts to an infinite canvas city.
items.detail: The skyline is cut from paper and scanned, then tinted to the palette at build time with its texture and shadow baked in. Seven layers move at their own depth with the pointer and the scroll, all driven by one requestAnimationFrame loop that sleeps when nothing moves. In front walks a linocut crowd by Clara Hidalgo: 30 figures in one sprite atlas, drawn on a canvas. Tap one and it jumps. With prefers-reduced-motion everything holds still.
